convincingly that S.’s shift into angry and open hostility was prompted by some veiled asper-

S.’s pamphlet A Proposal for Putting Reform to the Vote, published anonymously in 1817
as by ‘The Hermit of Marlow’, but with S. readily identifiable as the author. Thereafter S.’s
correspondence with and comments on Southey are uniformly hostile, and appear to derive
from a conviction that Southey was directly or indirectly responsible not only for all of the
attacks on his work and morality in the Quarterly, but also for the attack on Keats which S.
believed had killed him. S.’s drafts for the Preface to Adonais in Nbk 20 are overtly personal
